title: Bannock County adopts 180-day emergency moratorium on data center permits (Ordinance 2026-02)

facts.scope: receipt, processing and approval of applications for data centers
facts.exemptions: permits already issued, or applications already filed with the Board

summary: The Bannock County Board of Commissioners adopted an emergency 180-day moratorium on applications for data centers on July 30, 2026, citing imminent peril to water, environment, view sheds, decommissioning bonds, the grid and the aquifer. The county is directed to produce a permanent plan within 180 days.
source_title: Bannock County — Emergency Moratorium Ordinance No. 2026-02 (data centers)
verbatims: a moratorium is hereby imposed upon the receipt, processing, and approval of applications for data centers. This moratorium shall be in place for a period of one hundred and eighty (180) days following adoption of this moratorium.
This moratorium shall not apply to any permit that has already been issued
notes: Event date is OUTSIDE the 08-01 to 10-19 window; included as an untracked important action. Computed end 2027-01-26 (180 days from 07-30) matches a news report. Pocatello's 2026-07-20 denial of a $2.6B site was seen in search but is a site action for an untracked developer, not recorded.

title: Goldwater Institute says Pima County's 120-day data center pause is illegal

facts.challenger: Goldwater Institute (vice president for litigation Jon Riches)
facts.litigation_status: no case filed; Goldwater said it would consider representing an affected property owner

summary: On Sept. 29, 2026 the Goldwater Institute said Pima County's pause is illegal under Title 11 and Prop. 207 because the county cannot prove data centers are an imminent threat. The supervisor who sponsored it says the pause is based on Title 11. No lawsuit had been filed as of the report.
source_title: KJZZ — Goldwater Institute says Pima County data center moratorium is illegal
verbatims: says Pima County's four-month pause on data center development is illegal because it cannot prove data centers are an imminent threat
Allen says the moratorium is based on Title 11
notes: Challenge is a think-tank assertion, not a court ruling. Supervisor name in source is Jennifer Allen.

title: ACC approves joint cooperative framework for large-load electric service agreements

facts.instrument: joint application for ACC approval of electric service agreements between large-load customers and cooperatives

summary: The Arizona Corporation Commission unanimously approved a joint application by six electric cooperatives for a standardized large-load process. The process approves electric service agreements with large-load customers, such as data centers, and is framed as protecting existing ratepayers from bearing the infrastructure costs of that growth. This is a service-agreement framework, not a rate case.
source_title: Arizona Corporation Commission — ACC approves measure to ensure electric cooperative customers don't pay for large-load growth
verbatims: This procedure supports the Commission's "Growth Pays for Growth" approach when it comes to the addition of new large-load customers.
notes: Open meeting date 2026-08-12 per the ACC release URL and trade coverage; release posted 2026-08-13. Using 08-12 as the event date. Center Square describes it as rule changes; the ACC release describes a single joint-application approval, which this record follows. Not yet clear whether this is a tariff or a new service-agreement type; re-check the type on curation.

title: St. Charles Parish council rejects eight-month data center moratorium, 5-3

facts.proposed_end_condition: until the parish enacts specific data center regulations

summary: The St. Charles Parish council voted 5-3 against an eight-month moratorium on new data centers, after a debate on Monday, April 6, 2026. Supporters said it was needed to regulate location, size, water, energy and noise. The parish reported no current proposals for large data centers.
source_title: Herald Guide — Parish council rejects 8-month moratorium on new data centers

title: Baltimore County Council extends data center moratorium through end of 2027
summary: The Baltimore County Council unanimously passed a bill on Tuesday, Sept. 22, 2026 extending its moratorium on data centers through December 31, 2027. The bill does not set permanent rules; it extends the pause while the council considers Planning Board recommendations.
source_title: Baltimore Banner — Baltimore County data center moratorium
verbatims: The County Council unanimously passed a bill Tuesday night extending the county's moratorium on data centers through the end of 2027.

title: Coeur d'Alene council announces it will not approve data center proposals pending study

facts.mechanism: announcement/resolution of non-approval, not an ordinance or a moratorium
